reviews.title: 321URXW QD-OLED
reviews.content:
I purchased the MSI MPG 321URXW QD-OLED as an upgrade for both my gaming setup and media setup, coming from the MSI MAG 271QPX E2, and overall it has been one of the most impressive monitors I’ve owned. I use it daily with a PS5 Pro, gaming PC (RTX 4080), and Apple TV 4K, so I’ve had the chance to test it across competitive gaming (Apex Legends, BF6, Fortnite), cinematic titles (The Witcher 3, Ghost of Yotei, RDR2), and streaming content.

My favorite aspect is easily the QD-OLED panel. Compared to my previous 271QPX E2, the larger 32" 4K screen feels like a massive step up in immersion while keeping that same fast OLED responsiveness. Colors look incredibly rich without feeling oversaturated, blacks are truly black, and HDR makes highlights pop in a way that feels closer to a high-end OLED TV than a typical monitor. The white chassis looks clean on the desk next to my Logitech G715 & G705, and white Lian Li O11 Dynamic EVO PC case.

Pros:
• QD-OLED looks best on a monitor, in my opinion. Perfect blacks, responsive, and colorful without being too punchy.
• Simple UI, easy to navigate. Has many settings. I used the recommended settings by TFTCentral on YouTube.
• HDMI 2.1 bandwidth allows full console feature support
• Two HDR modes. I am currently using HDR1000.
• Surprisingly sharp text clarity for a QD-OLED panel
• Great for people who switch between PC and console like I do.
• 3-year warranty for burn-in.

Things to be aware of:
• I experienced a VRR color-cycling issue with PS5 Pro performance modes that MSI is reportedly addressing with the next update. After reverting to firmware 0.08, performance has been stable.
• There is no setting to adjust HDR brightness.
• As with many OLEDs, they don't get very bright. I tend to game in a darker room so it's no problem for me. However, you should have no issues unless you have a lot of direct light hitting the screen.
• These panels are more difficult to clean compared to a WOLED panel. I use the "MagicFiber Microfiber Cleaning Cloth" and "EVEO Screen Cleaner Spray Kit" from Amazon and it comes out like new. Be sure to be gentle. 

Overall, this monitor delivers stunning picture quality and excellent gaming performance. If you’re upgrading from a smaller OLED or moving from a traditional IPS panel, the jump in immersion and quality is immediately noticeable. This is my 4th OLED product (LG C1, C4, MSI 271QPX E-2) and will never go back to anything non-OLED. 
I chose this monitor over others mainly because I had great experience with my previous MSI monitor. If you want an OLED experience in a monitor form factor with strong console support, this is an easy recommendation.

q_a.question: Is a charger included in the box?
q_a.answer:
Battery charger is NOT included!  Are you kidding me?  Apparently nobody includes chargers any more.  OEM's love to hype their supposed fast charge capabilities, but don't bother giving you a charger capable of the claimed speed.  I found the Lenovo 68W charger (it's cheaper than their 45W) on sale through their website (it's currently out of stock), and it seems to work very well and consistently maintains a 40-42W charge rate.  A well known leading competitors 45W charger does not consistently maintain high speed charging, and after only a few seconds at 32-33W repeatedly resets dropping back down to 0W then slowly climbing back up  (per AccuBattery App).  

Minus 1 Star!  Yeah, yeah, I get the whole claimed e-waste excuse for not including a charger, but... 45W chargers are not old news, and not everybody has them laying around like the old standard 10W chargers.  New tech, lots of advertising and hype.  BUT... Hey! it's NOT INCLUDED in the package.

reviews.title: Beautiful & Blazing fast!
reviews.content: I am so happy with this purchase. I was lucky enough to see an ad for this laptop when it was still $1,299 and, boy, am I glad I pulled the trigger on this one, especially since the price has since risen to $1,999. I was specifically looking for a thin and light laptop with decent RAM capacity and, more specifically, LPDDR5X. The Low Power Double Data Rate memory is soldered directly on the board, very close to the processor, so it's blazing fast, and this thing has 32GB, which is more than enough for most people, even for gaming. When I researched LPDDR5X and discovered that the max transfer speed was 8533MT/s, I assumed that was just a theoretical upper limit. But Windows Task manager and the Performance tab reflect that, and I ran AIDA64 benchmarks immediately after receiving it, and it's quite fast, with a sustained read speed of 87808 MB/s and latency of 95.3 ns. AIDA64 GPGPU Benchmark showed single-precision FLOPS of 3974 and memory copy of 70.8 GB/s. These aren't anywhere near discreet GPU numbers in a desktop gaming rig, but it's pretty darned good for a shared-memory iGPU. I decided to try some light gaming, and installed Steam and Final Fantasy XIV. I was absolutely flabbergasted when it ran the game perfectly with most settings maxed out. If you do plan on gaming with this laptop, keep in mind that, as a thin and light laptop with an integrated GPU it's not meant to run AAA games. That being said, it does have 2 USB-C/Thunderbolt 4 ports, so you could (and plenty of people have) run it with an external GPU to get something approximating a desktop gaming experience. Speaking of I/O, I'm totally satisfied with what is included; 2 Thunderbolt ports, HDMI, only a single USB-A slot, a Micro SD card reader (which I will get plenty of use out of, transferring print files to a Bambu 3D printer), and, of course, WiFi and Bluetooth. The OLED screen has some of the richest color and deepest blacks I have seen in a laptop, but the screen is very glossy and tends to throw off a lot of glare in dark conditions or subdued ambient light. If you're watching YouTube or streaming in a dark room, you'll definitely see yourself reflected on screen. The battery is great, too. I had heard in a video somewhere that they estimated it could continuously display video for up to 23 hours on a single charge, depending on the power management settings. And let's talk about this lid. Wow. Each one is handcrafted by Japanese lacquerware artisans with a version of Hokusai's Great Wave Off Kanagawa, which anyone who is familiar with Japanese art or, more specifically, woodblock prints, will immediately recognize. It is absolutely beautiful, but it is also a fingerprint magnet, and they REALLY show up, so be prepared to constantly buff the lid with the microfiber cloth sandwiched between the keyboard and the screen. Everything about this laptop is a work of art. The box is beautiful, too, and opens in such a way that it tilts the back of the laptop up out of the box to make it very easy to remove carefully. It includes a pretty little mouse with similar lacquerware artistry, but I'm not sure if it's actual lacquerware; I left it in the box, along with the cool badge holder and the extended mousepad/deskpad with matching art. The bundled laptop sleeve is nothing fancy. It has a nice soft, velvety texture to it, but ZERO padding, so it's not something I will be using regularly. Instead, I will probably opt for one of the Thule hard-shell cases. I feel like this is one of those rare instances where an electronic device will continue to retain some value after purchase. Each one is numbered, but I'm not sure what the production runs are all about. Mine is numbered XXX/700 A, so perhaps there are several production runs (A, B, C, etc.), each 700, because I can't imagine they will only ever make 700 of these. MSI's own website mentions that it comes with "up to Intel® Core™ Ultra 9 processor(Series 2)", but I have only seen this version. That being said, I can't imagine there would be a noticeable difference in performance between the two specs. This thing is a work of art, inside and out, and I can't imagine anyone being unhappy after purchasing one. If you're in the market for a thin and light laptop, and your budget is flexible enough, go for it. This is probably the absolute best electronic device purchase I have ever made.

reviews.title: Amazing machine, both looks and function
reviews.content:
First off, you get some cool matching accessories: mousepad, mouse, luggage tag, etc. It's a nice inclusion which may not be obvious from the description.

The laptop itself looks amazing. This isn't just some sticker on the lid or whatever, it's actually got texture to it and appears to be lacquered. It actually looks better in person than the pictures.

Performance-wise, this machine is also top notch. It is powerful, has a great OLED display, nice port selection, and is extremely light. Battery lasts an incredible amount of time too - about 10 hrs of mixed use in my experience. It has an IR camera for Windows Hello, and the webcam (which is pretty decent) has a physical shutter built in.

RAM is not upgradeable, but it ships with 32GB which should be plenty for most. The SSD can be swapped (1 slot only). I dropped in a 2TB 970 EVO I had from a previous machine and, after some fumbling with drivers, got a clean Windows install up. Note on that: you should probably download the drivers from MSI's site to a USB beforehand if this is your only device and you want to do the same. 

I have only two minor complaints: the speakers aren't great, and the machine is a huge fingerprint magnet. 

With regards to the speakers, they do get loud but don't sound great. Bass in particular is lacking. This isn't a big deal for me as I don't usually use this for media, but others may find it a bigger problem.

The keys have that same lacquered finish as the lid, but both will show fingerprint marks very easily... and it's kind of hard to avoid touching either of those parts (especially the keys!) Let's just say there's a good reason they included a big microfiber cloth.

The only other thing to note is the top of the lid is a bit squishy. I wouldn't put anything heavy on it, but then again you probably wouldn't want to anyway as it might damage that super nice art on it.

Overall, I really like this device, though I'll admit a lot of it is just how nice it looks.

reviews.title: Best for Local LLMs + Gaming + Productivity
reviews.content:
I bought the ASUS ROG Z13 Flow with 128gb Unified RAM mainly for one purpose — "to run LLMs locally" — and honestly, it has exceeded my expectations.

I’ve downloaded and tried multiple models, and currently allocated 64 GB as VRAM to load "Gemma 4 26B Q4". I was honestly surprised by the speed. I’m getting around "42 – 45 tokens/sec", which I did not expect from a device this size. Really impressed with the performance.

My kids also loving it for gaming while I'm away from desk. On our previous laptop with 8 GB VRAM, we were getting 60 - 100 FPS in most of the games. With the Z13, we’re seeing 380+ FPS in the games we play. That’s a huge upgrade and the gaming performance is really impressive.

One thing that surprised me the most is how quiet the system is, even while gaming heavily. I was expecting a lot more fan noise and heat, but in my experience it has been surprisingly quiet and doesn’t get uncomfortably hot. This is especially nice when using it during a driving trip.

I also really like the detachable keyboard. With the USB ports and HDMI, it feels like much more than just a tablet. I can use it as a proper productivity machine when needed and then easily switch back to tablet mode.

Though its not OLED, with 500nit, 180hz refresh makes display a breeze... ultimate beauty with brain!

Overall, I’m really loving the Z13. The combination of local AI performance, gaming, portability, and the 2-in-1 design makes it a very impressive machine for what I wanted to use it for.

So far, I’m very happy with the purchase. Strongly recommend.

reviews.title: Very fast and responsive, but know its limits
reviews.content:
It is a very good, fast, and responsive machine. However, if you are looking at the 128GB version specifically for heavy AI workloads or high-end gaming, there are a few things you should know.
​I originally wanted to run large local LLMs. While the laptop is fully capable of running them, pushing anything above 30 to 38 billion parameters just isn't reasonable. The models will load, but the generation speed is far too slow to be practical. Because of this bottleneck, the 128GB version wasn't as useful to me as I hoped. If you want to run LLMs, a laptop with an RTX 5090 is a much better buy; it can run those same 30B+ models, but it will process them significantly faster.
​As for gaming, it is generally great, but it does have some frustrating restrictions. I ran into issues where certain AAA games were unplayable at medium settings. If your main focus is gaming, you will get a much better and more reliable experience out of a standard laptop equipped with an RTX 5070.
​Ultimately, it’s a cool and capable device, but you might be better off saving your money on the RAM upgrade and buying a dedicated gaming or AI laptop depending on your specific needs.

reviews.content: standing functionality in a compact laptop.  Love working remote with this beauty.

reviews.title: ZenBook Duo
reviews.content: Best travel laptop ever.  2 screens. Lighter than my old pc!

reviews.title: Fantastic laptop for digital nomads and travelers!
reviews.content: If you travel frequently and don't want to be burdened with lugging around a portable monitor, this laptop has the answer. It has plenty of power and the specs are great. The sound is amazing. The battery life is fantastic! The laptop transitions from traditional laptop to the dual screen setup seamlessly. All this with a lightweight laptop that will not way you down when you are on the go. Highly recommend this product especially for digital nomads who work from multiple locations.

reviews.title: 2 screens are so much better than one
reviews.content:
Asus has finally refined this dual screen laptop, after several earlier versions, to the point at which it seems do natural to work with the two screens that it is hard to go back to a regular laptop.  Previous versions of this or Lenovo's 9i had poor battery life and still seemed like they were beta testing. 

Every detail has been re-enginered.  The look and polished, smooth feel; opening the laptop with just one hand; topnotch displays that don't blind you with overhead light reflection, a nicely integrated pen.  

The only thing that reminds you that it isn't quite perfect are the occasional glitches when the keyboard is off the laptop and a screen background will go black, or the keyboard will lose connection.  Putting the keyboard back on the laptop solves it.  

Also, the first one they sent had a dead bottom screen that was a hardware, not a software issue

I normally don't  splurge on new laptops and usually wait until they have been out a year to buy them at discount.  But this one seems worth it.

reviews.title: Portable AI and Gaming Beast
reviews.content: Working great with Cachyos as a local AI playground and for steam gaming. Check out AMD's ai playbooks for strix halo. They have put quite a bit into making it easy to get ai workflows up and running fast. This processor is usually found in small desktops like the Framework desktop but in this form factor the power and portability you get is kind of insane. On linux you can easily get the 90 watt tdp or dial in a quiet portable power profile. Ditch Windows on this beast to get the most out of it. I'm using it as an always around ai hub. Great for testing ai workflows and managing other machines. With memory pricing as it is right now, the 64gb of ram at this speed is nice, should be good for a while. (hint: set reserved vram in the bios to the lowest value, 512mb, and linux will manage the allocation of system/gpu ram for you on the fly)

reviews.title: Amazing laptop
reviews.content: Runs like a dream the storage alone plus the ram make this laptop well worth the price

reviews.title: Great buy
reviews.content: I have had this laptop for a long while. I really like it, that key pad comes off so you could use like a tablet if you wanted. Does great gaming....love it

reviews.title: Amazing Device, Despite Windows 11 Bloat
reviews.content:
This tablet is of course extremely powerful. the most powerful tablet you can buy even in late 2026. It does handle more like a laptop however due to the weight and thickness, but the touch screen is amazing, and there's a lot of flexibility. It's relatively quiet though the fans are noticeable at top speeds, which will definitely kick in while gaming, so keep that in mind if you plan to use this with anyone else in the room. 

Most modern games play best in 1080p, which still looks great on the small screen, but not so great if you plan to doc on a larger monitor. If that's the plan, go with a true gaming laptop. This thing is meant to be portable, with gaming happening right on its screen, so it's all about massive power in a small form factor. 

All in all I'm extremely impressed with this device, and it's coming with me on all my travels. The star I docked is due to Windows bloat, and of course the extreme price. However if you can afford it and manage your expectations, it's a truly impressive gaming device.

reviews.title: Wow. Replaced my MacBook Pro, iPad, & SteamDeck!
reviews.content:
This device truly delivered. Really wanted to consolidate all of my devices both for travel and simplicity. Was considering the Microsoft Surface heavily until a Best Buy associate listened to my use case and recommended the Z13 Flow. I wasn’t sure it was for me at first but after a little research I decided to pull the trigger and committed to giving it a fair shot.

Super glad I did. The device performs amazing well all around and for those that travel, the detachable keyboard with kickstand is a massive win both for gaming and media watching modes. Battery life is overall very efficient in travel modes/setting and no problem with media use on long haul flights. Naturally plug it in when you can.

Device feels very premium and performs incredibly well across all use cases!

reviews.title: 2 LEMONS in a row
reviews.content: The first one I purchased lasted an entire 6 days before it completely crashed and would not turn on. The replacement lasted less than 24 hours with the same issue and was so hot when it crashed that the store clerk noticed how hot it still was after it had been powered off for 45 minutes. I could have been extremely unlucky, but overall I would say this model is a total piece of TRASH. 0/10 If I could leave a negative star rating, I would.

reviews.title: Worth the purchase?
reviews.content:
Short answer yes.

People immediately point out the battery life being 6-8 hours off the charger and very dependent whether your doing office/school work or gaming. As everyone points out, gaming, you’ll get 2 hours or less depending on your settings and how many apps are running. I find it just good enough for half my school day full time until I need to plug it in when it’s on low battery. Probably could save battery with messing with the settings, but it’s alright. 

Another argued issue is the screen, some say, paying 2k and or more should have OLED. For an IPS touch screen, it’s pretty good. I have no issues playing plugged in or not plugged in. Obviously if you’re plugged in you can play at a higher graphics quality. 

I do college work on the Z13 and play titles like Total War Warhammer 3, Space Marine 2, and Arc Raiders. No issue there “when plugged in”

It’s portable, it’s powerful, and it’s just hitting every itch. 

Side Note: I have a ASUS ROG Falchion RX low profile…wayyy better for gaming when gaming instead of the actual Z13 touch pad keyboard.

reviews.title: Great purchase
reviews.content: Amazingly fast and love the form factor. Bought this to run local LLMs and it does that without sweating. Tested the latest Qwen 3.8 works like a charm.

reviews.title: Powerful, Portable, and Worth It!
reviews.content: I absolutely love the ROG Flow Z13! The performance is incredible, and it handles everything I throw at it with no problem. The 180Hz display looks amazing—everything is super smooth, sharp, and responsive. I also really like how portable it is considering how much power it has. The 64GB of memory is awesome for multitasking, gaming, and heavier programs. The touchscreen and 2-in-1 design make it even more versatile. Overall, it feels like a premium, powerful machine that I can take anywhere. Definitely one of my favorite tech purchases, and I would highly recommend it!

reviews.title: Absurdly powerful tablet
reviews.content: This thing generally blows through games and AI workloads pretty easily.  Im getting ~90 fps in Cyberpunk at native resolution (with all the FSR trickery anyway) and running some pretty large local models.  Battery life is about what you'd expect from this sort of thing.  You want a battery that lasts all day, buy a Mac.  This is not that. Windows still sucks at hibernation/sleep but I can deal with that to have something the size of a Microsoft Surface with 64GB of ram and a very serviceable graphics chipset. I actually really like the keyboard feel as well.  Keys are solid.

reviews.title: God Tier
reviews.content:
The only gaming tablet/laptop you'll ever need in my opnion.
It is so portable,so powerful (64GB of RAM!!!!)  

The fact that you can game and its equivalent to the RTX 4080.

If your getting this get the 64GB or the 128GB.

The 32GB is not worth it.

reviews.title: Great device albeit niche
reviews.content: This device is awesome. While obviously not the best bang for your buck in terms of performance, the tablet form factor makes it very portable and the fact it can keep this portability with this amount of performance is outstanding. The screen is beautiful and the IPS panel honestly doesn’t differ much than my OLED monitor outside of blacks. Small nitpick with the amount of glare from sunlight but it’s not like this is a device that’s supposed to be used outside. The only major con that I feel really matters is the battery life (outside of gaming) which you’d expect to be better on a device running on integrated graphics, in which doing school work or web browsing only netted around 5-6 hours of battery life.

reviews.title: Great Device for Price
reviews.content: It's a great device for the price right now. Using for local AI stuff and it's miles better than something that does not have dedicated graphics. The tablet form factor works better than I expected. Lots of horse power in a small-ish package.

reviews.title: Laptop
reviews.content: Amazing product. Great for all needed tasks. Performance and the convenience of becoming a tablet is outstanding.

reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.content: - ROG Flow Z13 13.4 is the be best laptop/tablet. No issues best purchase I've ever made

q_a.question: Hey I've been researching this thing the best I can from what I've gathered it has the readeon 8060s which is entry level? everything i see compares it to the rtx 4070 thus the 4070 must be entry level or is amd claims of the igpu performance false?
q_a.answer:
Its an RDNA3.5 40CU iGPU with a relatively low TDP limit sharing up to 120W. It'll likely perform comparably to a desktop RX 7600 because of that. CPU wise, its effectively a TDP limited 9950x with quad channel 8000MT/sec RAM. Zen5 does great at low TDPs but still wants ~40W per CCD for optimal core clock boosting.

In this device specifically, it appears to have an 80W TDP limit which is about middle of the 45-120W range its capable of. That will be the limitation on the Max+ 395. Doesn't mean it won't perform amazingly, just more of a limitation than I was hoping as a USB4 eGPU host.

reviews.title: An Excellent Machine for Essentially Anyone
reviews.content:
As an average user that sometimes games and sometimes uses GIS software (which requires decent CPU power), this device absolutely slaughters everything I can throw at it. 

First off, the form factor for me is fairly perfect. It can fit into fairly small bags and has an extremely color accurate screen, with the 180 hz refresh rate it's extremely smooth. 
The CPU heavy tasks I throw at it are nothing, its as if the PC hums along without thinking, even on battery. I did spend some time allocating VRAM and understanding undervolting and things of that sort, which I know improves performance. 

As far as gaming, I havent found a game this thing can't run at good settings. I am always plugged in when gaming, since the one time I did game while on battery, it lasted about an hour. I think this thing works best on battery. 

Battery life does last quite a while on general tasks, I would say about 5 to 6 hours, but then on heavy tasks, I would just plug in because this thing will eat up your power. 

I think overall, this is a great machine, and definitely can fill multiple roles for many different people, but I would absolutely recommend it for pretty much anyone, because it should last you quite a while, and it's compact enough that you wont feel as though youre lugging around a gaming laptop.

reviews.title: A Great College Pick
reviews.content:
Coming from a college student that used to haul two apple products at a time, I genuinely would recommend this laptop over those, especially at this price point. The X Plus chip is still a powerful and long-lasting battery, even if it's a year old (at the time of writing this review). The OLED screen makes me want to watch more movies and the size of the display isn't an issue at the slightest. It's portable and feels solid, compared to laptops around the same price point. The speakers aren't bad for casual use either, but it feels like it gets flat the louder it is. (FYI I am not an audiophile, so take that comment with a grain of salt)

If you are a person who prefers to handwrite notes and also draw, I would recommend getting this laptop-- albeit the drawing function is finicky, if you can look past it, it still gets the job done and is still reliable. You could get an inexpensive stylus on other marketplaces and it'll work. (I recommend the Metapen brand)

Some of the gripes that I have with this device is the kickstand, the keyboard, and how the ports are laid out:

You lose out on comfortably resting it on your lap, but a good work around is flipping the keyboard and having the stand rest on the keyboard, making it bearable, although it will act as a tablet.

The keyboard is reliable and easy to type on. I got used to it in a matter of a few seconds, but the touchpad is a little annoying. If you're resting your hands on the empty spaces of the keyboard and the surface isn't even, it'll register random left clicks, which hurts it's score.

The stylus holder is practically a tiny sleeve that holds it on the side of the laptop. It feels a little flimsy, and with how this sleeve is placed, it sometimes gets in the way of the ports to charge. 

I really wish they would give us more customization with how the laptop looks. The case it comes with is a dull green, which may make people dislike it. If they would make it black (I believe they made the new PZ14 black), it would have probably been a more popular option-- or if they sold different color cases.

I recommend this laptop if you:
Want a laptop that can draw, write, and have touchscreen versatility.
Want a beautiful display to enjoy movies, videos, and digital creation.
Want a Surface Pro without the Surface Pro price tag.

Now this is an ARM64 chipset, which means it's not compatible with all programs, compared to Ryzen and Intel's x86 chipsets. If you're playing games, I wouldn't recommend this, I haven't even tried any video games on it yet. I would look up ARM64 vs x86 to decide on a Snapdragon CPU or a Intel/AMD CPU.

reviews.title: Great for notes
reviews.content:
I got the PZ13 mainly for note-taking, and for that purpose, it actually does its job. The pen works well enough to get through classes, write notes, and keep everything organized digitally. It’s responsive most of the time, and once you get into a flow, it feels pretty natural.

That said, it’s not perfect. Sometimes the pen input can be a little inconsistent, and palm rejection isn’t always reliable, which can interrupt your writing here and there. A lot of that comes down to Windows—it’s just not as polished for pen and touch as you’d expect from a dedicated tablet experience.

Even with those quirks, it still works for what I need. I can take notes, sketch things out, and keep everything in one place without carrying notebooks around. So while it’s a little funky at times, especially because of Windows, it gets the job done for note-taking, which is what I bought it for in the first place.

reviews.title: Long battery life, awesome speed, very versatile
reviews.content: It took some getting used to, but now I am in absolute love with this laptop. Initially I was bothered by the weight ratio and odd magnetic "kickstand" and the lack of USB ports. But with some accessorizing (there's a second Type C next to the SD slot that I can plug a small hub into) and time, I've come to adapt. The laptop is surprisingly quick and the battery last an astonishingly long time. The touchscreen is super sensitive, but it's meant to be this way for people to effectively draw on the screen. Palm rejection is apparently a feature, but I've yet to have it function for me (maybe a setting I'm missing?) because I'm constantly clicking on things with my hand. Again, I'm chalking this up to a learning curve. I have run into a few compatibility issues because the CPU is ARM, so some x86 applications do not function properly, but nothing that is a deal breaker.  Many times, I just have to hunt down ARM versions of the software I need.

From the moment I unboxed the Asus ProArt PZ13 OLED 3K Detachable Laptop, I knew I was holding something special. This device seamlessly blends stunning design, powerhouse performance, and professional-grade visuals into one truly exceptional package.

For Creators & Professionals

The detachable form factor gives me flexibility I didn’t know I needed — tablet mode for sketching and on-the-go work, and laptop mode when it’s crunch time. Performance is smooth and responsive even with demanding creative apps open.

Performance & Productivity
Apps launch instantly and multitasking is effortless. The keyboard is comfortable for long typing sessions, and the overall build feels premium and durable. Battery life is impressive for such a capable machine — I can get through most of my day without hunting for a charger.

Smart Design
Lightweight yet solid, this feels like the future of portable creative tech. It’s perfect for anyone who wants creative horsepower without sacrificing mobility — from filmmakers and photographers to digital artists and designers.

Bottom Line
The Asus ProArt PZ13 OLED 3K Detachable is a standout device that earns every one of its five stars. If you’re looking for a versatile, high-performance laptop with a gorgeous display and creative-friendly features, this is absolutely one of the best options on the market

reviews.title: Solid PC, no pen included? How?!
reviews.content:
I waited a long time for this device to release, extremely excited for a Surface Pro alternative with more power, all of the features I was looking for in a creative-centered device in the most flexible form factor available. The PC overall is exactly what I was hoping for, but with one massive miss. 

All marketing for this PC included the stylus, the ASUS Pen 3.0, and stressed the quality, functionality, and experience. I was absolutely blown away to open the box after ordering on release day to find no stylus included. Something had to be wrong, as every review I'd seen had the stylus included in the box, and it's use was so aggressively advertised everywhere I'd seen reference to the PC. It's a tablet Windows PC, after all, designed for creatives. The rear cover has the pen holder integrated. There's no way that they'd sell it in other markets including the stylus, but leave it out in the US, right?

I reached out to ASUS and they confirmed that the model number includes the stylus. Connected with Best Buy per ASUS's recommendation and was told that it's not part of the package. Reach back out to ASUS, open tickets, multiple phone calls, chat sessions, emails, and finally received a response that they do NOT include the Pen 3.0 in the US release. When I expressed my frustration and asked what the solution would be, I was told that it's not available to purchase on it's own. I couldn't possibly be more blown away at how horrible of a decision this is on the part of ASUS. To then be told "we're sorry, that's frustrating, have a good day" by ASUS support has completely changed my view of the company. 

I've owned ASUS products for many, many years. This is very likely to be my last, if I end up keeping it. I wouldn't have questioned the purchase for a moment if it was $50 more and included the stylus, I can't wrap my head around the decisions made that lead to the exclusion of it in this package. Beyond that, to have absolutely zero solution in place for a customer to purchase the Pen 3.0 just shows that the priority isn't on the customer experience and overall satisfaction, and when ASUS misses the mark, they don't really care. 

If you value the ability to use a stylus that integrates well into the package (I've purchase a third party device that rattles around in the compartment as the magnetic point isn't in the right location) you'll want to look elsewhere. Of course, there are older versions of ASUS pens available, but they're expensive and fall short of the intended experience per ASUS's marketing. Spend a bit more for a very similar Surface Pro option where you have to buy your own keyboard and pen? Buy a more "standard laptop" configuration? I'm not sure of the answer as this was so very close to my perfectly ideal solution, but as of this moment I'm unable to use the device in the way that I was lead to believe I'd be able to.

reviews.title: Lightweight laptop with excellent screen
reviews.content:
Been using this laptop for the past two months. I am very happy with the light weight and excellent screen. Coming from a MacBook Pro 16", the speakers are worse, but not bad still. 
Keep in mind that the HDMI, despite being marked as 2.1, is 2.1 TDMS, meaning it cannot output at 4K 120 Hz.

reviews.title: Great laptop
reviews.content: Fast reliable laptop that does the job. 48GB memory is a huge plus for the Zenbook.

reviews.title: Over the top
reviews.content: This laptop is fast, clean, sleek, lite, crisp. It is the best one I have had.

reviews.title: A few issues but still a cut above the rest!
reviews.content:
Not new to Asus brand, but first timer for the Zenbook and it’s very nice.  A true standout feature of the A16 is how lightweight it is compared to any other slim designed laptop I’ve had.  Its aluminum alloy chassis is a key factor to its weight but it still feels like it’s pretty sturdy.  Zabriskie Beige is an interesting color choice for a laptop, but I actually like it.  It gives it a unique and subdued elegance look.

The keyboard is pretty basic with good spacing between the keys, but why is the trackpad so ridiculously big, I don’t know.  I have to adjust the way I rest my hands to avoid accidental touches and clicks.  And I would prefer it if it had 10-key numeric keypad and that the Insert and Delete didn’t share a button.  It does have a backlit keyboard which is one of my must-haves.

This Zenbook is a cut above the rest with the number of ports it comes with.  Two USB-C, one of which is used for charging; a USB-A, a HDMI, an audio jack, and lo and behold, an SD card slot! 

And the 16” OLED 3K display is just beautiful!  Clear lines and vibrant color, no distortions or underlying shadows, making videos, pictures, and graphics, not gaming quality, but still very pleasing.  The speakers on the other hand are pretty flat and could be better.

The Snapdragon X2 Elite Extreme partnered with the 48GB RAM provides good CPU performance for the most part, but I have encountered compatibility issues with some of the specialized software I use.  This seems to be a common problem with ARM processors and Windows Home platforms in my experience.   Battery life is great though and lasts all day. I was able to go 7.5 hours before needing to charge it.

Even with its issues though, the Asus Zenbook A16 is a beautiful laptop with premium features and enhancements that make it a worthwhile investment.

reviews.title: Solid thin and light laptop with good performance
reviews.content:
The laptop is very thin and very light with a nice satin finish. Overall build quality is high with the exception that the screen is a little flimsy, not problematic, just be aware of it.

The screen is wonderful, HDR, OLED. Does ok in light, no glare protection film.

Processor speed is kinda ridiculous for the form factor. You are compromising a little on software compatibility, if you're unfamiliar look up ARM architecture. I haven't run into compatibility issues myself and emulation has come a long way anyway. 48GB of ram is insane in this market and should be future proof for a long time. Only downside on performance is that the GPU is just alright. Definitely enough for light gaming, and that situation should improve as Qualcomm becomes more of a market consideration for game developers.

Battery like is great but not best of the best. For so much processing power you can really get a lot of life out of this thing. It will go about 8-10 hours of web browsing. Running full tilt you'll probably get 2-3 hours away from the wall. Not quite as good as other ARM laptops can offer, but that's the price you pay for so much performance. Also have noticed the battery drain during sleep is really low due to Qualcomms experience in the mobile industry. S0ix sleep ("Modern Standby") doesn't leave your laptop burning up in a bag like it can on traditional Intel and AMD based laptops. Though they have also improved in recent years.

Overall very happy with the laptop. If you are a professional that needs CPU performance but doesn't want to lug around a heavy 'desktop replacement' style laptop then this is an impressive option. Just be aware of the fee small caveats.

reviews.title: Very Responsive
reviews.content: No hiccups so far. Speed on the laptop is top tier. Build quality feels great. Screen display is crisp. Price is reasonable on a sale in this day and age.

reviews.title: A wonderful laptop but SSD upgrade NOT possible.
reviews.content:
The Good: Beautiful laptop. Powerful. Apps run well, even video processing is in par with intel/amd laptops with separate video processor. Plenty of I/O. Perfect laptop for both purpose, Primary or On the GO.
The Issue: NO SSD upgrade.
Laptop has OEM partitions. Gold standard by Microsoft has 4 partitions. System in partition 1, OS in 3 and WinRE in 4. This laptop has 16 partitions. System in 12 and OS in 14. After cloning to a larger SSD, Windows won't boot since it does not know where the system and OS partitions are. Hence, bcdboot has to apply which helps locating System and OS. The results, <1> slow booting & shutdown, <2> NO reset as WinRE gone, <3> NO Rescue Media. Windows still run, but not as perfect as it supposes to be. With regret, I had to return.

reviews.title: Everything I need and more
reviews.content: I bought this laptop for college, and I am glad I chose it. I can write my reports, record presentations, sync to my phone, search documents by description (if I forget the title of the saved file), and so much more. I love it. I highly recommend this laptop for anyone who needs a multi-purpose computer.

reviews.title: Slim, Lightweight, Incredible Display and Speed
reviews.content:
I am a HUGE fan of ASUS Zenbooks,  I have had a few 14” and this is my first 16” version.  Even the larger device is super lightweight.  Right out of the box you will want to allow some time to set up the device and install updates.  Just plug it in during this process so it is fully charged when it is done updating.  The wel;come screens walk you through all the steps.  This is so easy to set up, just be patient and allow time for a few restarts while the software updates along the way.

While it is updating you can enjoy the incredible screen and graphics.  There are nice tips and tutorials along the way to help you discover some of the incredible features of this device.  I prefer dual monitors when possible but I need something portable for my job so this 16” display is a nice balance. I can split the screen and have one tab or application on the left and a separate one on the right and I still have plenty of viewing real estate.  The keyboard has back lit keys which is incredibly useful especially in low light conditions.  The keys are minimal and super responsive and the trackpad is just plain awesome.  Plenty of room for my hands to rest to the sides of the track pad as well without interfering or accidentally touching the trackpad.

I use this primarily for productivity with a lot of web based applications and storage.  SO far i have had no issues with memory or speed or any lagging.  The processor can handle multiple tabs and apps at one time. I have been doing a lot lately with AI and Google Sheets and I have impressed with the processing speeds.  If there is one concern it seems the battery life drains a little quickly but that also could be me keeping the brightness on high all the time.  It is not an issue but I feel like it could be a little longer before it runs into Low Power mode.  If you are looking for a great school or work related computer that can travel easily with you this is a no brainer.  It is slim and lightweight and has a very impressive screen.

reviews.title: Cool Color, Gorgeous Screen, Compute Powerhouse
reviews.content:
TLDR:  Powerhouse Processor with GORGEOUS OLED screen

PROS
HUGE Generational Leap in Processing Power
Top-Rated RAM Speeds
Good Battery Life
Beige - Sounds Ugly.  Looks Great.
Beautiful 3K OLED Touchscreen

CONS
Ho Hum Backlit Keyboard
Huge Power Brick
Only a Gen 4 NVMe Drive

CONNECTIONS / PORTS
1 x HDMI 2.1
2 X USB-C
1 x USB-A 3.2
SD Card Slot
3.5mm Headphone Jack

SET-UP
ARM-based PC's have definitely evolved over the past year or so.  I remember when I got last generation's ARM-based laptop to review and while most things worked without issue, there were still some lingering issues with apps.

Another year of maturing has made making the switch to a Snapdragon processor much less of an issue as more and more programs work just as they would with any X86 processor.  Whether they be dedicated ARM-based apps or apps that run from within a Windows container, it is seamless to the end user.  While I did find a few programs that didn't work correctly last year when the first wave of ARM-based processors rolled out, I am happy to report that any and all apps I use on a regular basis are now fully compliant with the ARM architecture.

The new ZenBook is a welcome change from some of Asus' competitors.  It ships with minimal bloatware.  The only non-standard app installed is the MyAsus app.  It is a necessary install as it is the buyer's central repository of updates, warranty registration, and diagnostic suite.  The MyAsus app immediately greeted me with a critical update for the system bios.  In typical Asus fashion, the update (separate from Windows Updates) went without issue.

PERFORMANCE
How does the new Snapdragon X2 Elite hold up?  To find out, I ran a suite of tests comparing it to last year's Snapdragon X Elite and the current generation of Snapdragon X Plus processors.

The new Snapdragon X2 Elite holds a huge generational improvement compared to last year's top-of-the-line X Elite.  More cores, more throughput, faster RAM.  Differences from year to year are staggering.  The new X2 Elite handily beats its predecessor, often dramatically so.  Synthetic benchmarks are below:

Snapdragon X2 Elite:          44883 (91st Percentile)
Snapdragon X Elite 2025:  15976 (46th Percentile)
Snapdragon X Plus 2026:  18765 (55th Percentile)

SCREEN
The extra 1k of resolution on the new ZenBook is a welcome addition compared to last year's 2k OLED offerings.  Resolution increases from 1920 x 1200 up to 2880 x 1800.  The increase in resolution is immediately noticeable, especially with a nearly bezel-less 16" display.  Texts, images, graphics, everything is much crisper than a 2k screen.  Not to mention the new screen offers up to 1100 nits at peak brightness.  By far, the brightest, most dynamic display I've used to date.

BATTERY LIFE
I am averaging a good 7 hours of battery life of mixed use.  This is with the screen at approximately 50% brightness, all drivers updated, Windows Power Management set to Balanced, HDR disabled, and refresh rate capped at 60Hz.  I could possibly eek out a bit more, but at the cost of my enjoyment.  The improvements in processor efficiency are apparent.  The increased power demands of the 3K screen are easily offset in the improvements in processing efficiency.

FINAL THOUGHTS
While I was a bit hesitant last year when the first Snapdragon chips hit the market, I am far less skeptical now.  A full year of app development and processor refinement have got the Snapdragons on level playing field.

I am impressed at the HUGE speed increase over the previous generation of Snapdragon processors.  The X2 Elite has a whopping 18 cores of compute power and is teamed with some of the fastest LPDDR5X RAM I've seen to date.

While ARM-based processors were in their infancy last year, the ecosystem has grown and matured greatly in just a year's time.  I see no reason to be concerned about the ARM-based architecture and not give the ZenBook the highest 5-Star rating.

HIGHLY RECOMMENDED

reviews.title: Good potential
reviews.content:
The Asus Zenbook A16 has a lot to love about it with some minor drawbacks. 

I think the design is awesome. The current trend in laptop design is sleek minimalism which this laptop follows. I love the minimal branding. There are not any loud design elements but it still draws attention. One thing that you immediately will notice as you take it out of the box is the weight. This thing is unbelievably light. The chassis is made of an aluminum alloy called Ceraluminum. The texture is a bit...different. It feels like a smooth rock with the graininess rather than just smooth metal. Build quality feels ok. I think it's definitely much more sturdy than what the weight suggests. Asus claims it is very scratch-resistant. I obviously have not and will not put it to the test but time will tell. The hinge feels premium. You can open with one hand and it is sturdy. 

The port selection is above average in my opinion. It has two USB-C ports, a USB-A, an actually SD card slot, HDMI, and even an audio jack! For most people, I feel like you have enough where you don't need dongle/adapters so that is a plus. 

The keyboard is ok. It isn't anything extraordinary but it gets the job done. The trackpad is gigantic. Apple really started this trend of gigantic track pads. I think it's a nice novelty but if not done correctly then it can really get annoying. I actually did get some accidental palm clicks and ghost touches which was frustrating. I think smaller trackpads can be much more practical and still look good. 

The display is gorgeous.  I mean it is OLED. It is 3K. It is 120Hz. If you come from an IPS panel, it is a giant upgrade. Things were a joy to watch. Speakers were actually disappointing. You have to compare this with other premium level laptops like the Macbook and it does fall a bit short here. 

In terms of performance, the Snapdragon X2 Elite Extreme is both a positive and a minus. In terms of pure CPU performance, it is a monster of a chip. It comes paired with 48GB of RAM. The integrated graphics card is not as impressive and can be a rate-limiting factor but otherwise on paper this thing rocks. However, the biggest weakness comes from software compatibility. As it is an ARM processor, there are certain apps in Windows that will not run. I wasn't able to get certain games to run as well as some specialized software from work. Basic browsers, Microsoft apps, etc. run ok but for people who just need those basic things then there are far better and cheaper options out there. Alot of the premium for this laptop is brought on by the high performance but applying that high performance can feel limited in scope. There is a lot of potential obviously but it feels like you can't utilize it all. Battery life is good and easily gets you through a full day. 

All in all, the Asus Zenbook A16 can perform like a beast. It looks good and the display is gorgeous. However, it is still an ARM processor and has some compatibility issues with Windows.

reviews.title: Great laptop!

I am blown away by this Asus ZenBook laptop. It's super light, I believe, due to its Ceraluminum chassis and so thin. It's a hybrid material fusing lightness and strength of aluminum with the hard, scratch-resistant qualities of ceramic. It feels amazing and I love the color. 

The 3k display has up to double the pixels of a 2k display and the screen type is OLED. The display is very crisp, clear and bright with fantastic color. I can view it on my lap without my glasses. I love that! I also love that it is a touchscreen.  I don't use the touchscreen feature often but it's great to have.

I easily noticed the performance capability of the RAM during an initial windows update. The malicious tools update is always one that takes forever to complete. I noticed this one completed in only a minute or two. I've been able to really utilize AI with the large number of projects I have in my business. 

The keyboard and trackpad are good quality. They feel like they handle everything with just the right pressure input.

The sound could be a little louder but the quality and depth is great. The battery life: I used it probably 10 hours before needing to charge it again. The only other thing I could complain about is the size of the SSD. Feels like 1TB would have been perfect for this beast.


This beast of a laptop has handled everything I pushed at it with ease. I love this machine and I would absolutely recommend it to anyone.

reviews.title: A powerful 16-inch Copilot PC that is very light!
reviews.content:
The ASUS Zenbook A16 stands out with a great combination of Snapdragon X2 Elite Extreme processor, 48GB RAM, 1TB SSD and a 16" 3K OLED touchscreen, all packed into a laptop weighing under 3 lbs. This is my first laptop with 48GB RAM, and naturally I was curious to see what I could do with all that memory beyond my normal productivity apps. I started playing around with my Adobe content creation software (Firefly) along with Copilot and my usual work applications to see how far I could push it.

Having used both Intel and previous-generation Snapdragon Copilot+ PCs, I was particularly interested in the new X2 Elite Extreme. The first-generation Snapdragon laptops impressed me mostly with battery life and power efficiency. With the X2 Elite Extreme, Qualcomm seems to be pushing much harder on performance and AI while still keeping the efficiency advantage of the Snapdragon processor.

What Stood Out
Snapdragon X2 Elite Extreme + 48GB RAM:
The 18-core Snapdragon X2 Elite Extreme comes with an 80 TOPS NPU for AI workloads. The 48GB RAM is what caught my attention right away. I typically have Teams, multiple browser windows, Excel, PowerPoint, ChatGPT, Claude, and Copilot open at the same time, and 48GB gives you plenty of room for this kind of multitasking.

I also used my Adobe content creation software to put a little more load on the system instead of just testing Office applications. Content creation is where the extra memory starts to make more sense, especially when you are working with larger photos or video files while still having other applications running in the background. This is the kind of use case where I would rather have 48GB than the 16GB that is still common on many premium laptops.

The 80 TOPS NPU gives the laptop a lot more dedicated AI processing capability. Features such as Windows Studio Effects, Live Captions and other supported AI functions can run on the NPU instead of putting everything on the CPU. For me, that is the real value of the NPU supported AI features can run in the background while I continue working on everything else. Interestingly, while monitoring the NPU in Task Manager, I rarely saw utilization go beyond about 25% during my normal mix of productivity and background AI applications, which suggests there is still plenty of room for more demanding AI workloads.

16" 3K OLED Display
The 2880 x 1800 OLED touchscreen with a 120Hz refresh rate is easily one of the highlights of this laptop. The vibrant colors and sharp text make it great for reviewing dashboards, presentations, photos and watching videos. The 120Hz refresh rate also makes scrolling through webpages and documents noticeably smoother than a regular 60Hz display.
I really like the larger 16-inch screen for productivity. There is enough screen space to keep two applications open side by side without immediately looking for an external monitor. It is very useful when working on PowerPoint, Excel, dashboards or Adobe content where the extra screen real estate makes a difference.
The OLED display also complements the content creation side of this laptop. Photos and videos look great on the 3K screen, and having a touchscreen is handy for quick navigation.

Lightweight Design
For a 16-inch laptop, the weight is probably the biggest surprise. At under 3 lbs, it feels more like carrying a 14-inch ultrabook than a traditional 16-inch laptop. I travel quite a bit and usually like having a larger screen or a portable monitor, but I don't like carrying a 4-5 lb laptop + monitor around. The A16 gives me both. The Zabriskie Beige finish is also a nice change from the typical gray or black laptops I currently own, and it gives the laptop a sleek, premium look.

AI, Productivity and Content Creation
The combination of the 80 TOPS NPU and 48GB RAM is what makes this laptop more interesting to me than just another thin Copilot+ PC. For normal productivity, 48GB is probably more than most people need today, but once you start adding content creation, AI applications and heavier multitasking, that extra memory becomes useful.
For my use, this is a good combination for Teams, Office applications, Copilot, browser-heavy workloads and Adobe content creation. The full-size SD card reader is another nice touch as I am constantly transferring photos and videos from my Drone and Osmo.

Connectivity and Ports
• 2x USB 4 Type-C
• USB-A
• HDMI 2.1
• Full-size SD card reader
• 3.5mm audio jack
• Wi-Fi 7
• Bluetooth 5.4
I like that ASUS kept the HDMI, USB-A and full-size SD card reader. I travel with enough adapters already, so having these ports built into such a thin laptop is definitely useful.

Things to Be Aware Of
This is still a Windows-on-ARM laptop, so I would check compatibility if you rely on older or specialized software. I couldn't get my 4 year old canon laser printer to run on this laptop due to driver compatibility issue. Mainstream Windows applications have come a long way on Snapdragon PCs, but there are still some legacy applications and games that may not work exactly the same way as they do on an Intel or AMD laptop. The newer Adreno graphics make this much more capable for gaming than the first-generation Snapdragon PCs, but I am still using this primarily for productivity, 3D design software and video editing software. 

Overall Impression
The Zenbook A16 has a great balance of performance, display size and portability. It’s a powerhouse for productivity, multitasking, content creation and AI applications. What impresses me the most is that ASUS managed to put all of this into a 16-inch laptop weighing under 3 lbs. For someone who travels frequently, wants a large OLED display and runs a mix of productivity, Copilot and content creation applications, this is a very compelling laptop.

reviews.title: The ASUS A16 sets the bar for productivity laptops
reviews.content:
I have a kid headed off to college who has been eyeing my laptop, so for this reason I found myself taking a jump from my current touch screen laptop to the ASUS Zenbook A16. This review is based on a week of use both at work and in my home office. 

TL:DR - This Zenbook gives other top line productivity focused laptops some strong competition. The build is sleek, refined looking, while still being robust without being heavy. The performance for productivity tools is top notch, not bogging down and not blowing through battery life. The OLED touchscreen monitor may be the best laptop touchscreen you've ever seen and the processor took every big task I threw at it without even the slightest lag.

Pros:
I love the keyboard weighting and layout. The keys are soft, quiet, and the perfect weight.
The design is a great mix of sturdiness and polish so it looks and feels high quality.
This may be the first time I've ever considered laptop speakers a pro, and while these still have opportunities for depth, they aren't bad. I can fill a medium sized bedroom room with music, or watch a movie without headphones and still enjoy the audio quality. 
The ASUS control panel puts key settings and functionality controls in one spot for quick setting adjustments.
This may be the best laptop on the market for power consumption versus performance. 

Cons:
Being really picky, I wish the screen would lay flat or have a tablet mode versus go to ~140 degrees.
The volume booster setting is complete garbage, and takes speaker performance back down to being flat and overdriven.

In the box is the Zenbook, instructions, and power cable. Setup is fantastically quick, no bloatware to load, just the normal Windows workflow and optional ASUS registration. Moving on to the performance, starting with the obvious, this OLED immediately grabs your attention at 3k resolution, 120Hz refresh rate and 500 nits brightness. The A16 build spec is such that you don't have to trade off battery life for brightness or touchscreen response for graphics performance. The real estate is well used, with a large touch pad, decent key spacing, and adequate ports around the perimeter (HDMI, 2 x USB-C Thunderbolt, audio jack, USB-A, and a card reader). The built in camera and microphone perform well for video conferencing, and the camera resolution (1080p) far exceeds expectations. Note that this is all packaged into a laptop that weighs in under 3 lbs.

The Qualcomm ARM-based Snapdragon X2 Elite Extreme chip is a powerhouse for energy efficiency and AI tasks, since this isn't really a gaming build, I ran a web based stress testing tool to see if I could find performance gaps because I could not get this laptop to bog down when running macros while using 3d printing software. During the stress testing I found was that if I had the keyboard backlight on full power, the keyboard got hot and the laptop base had a small amount of heat but zero signs of processor stress (lag, apps not responding or crashing) or what I consider to be unacceptable levels of overheating. What surprised me was there was almost no fan noise. When I turned off the keyboard lighting the heat was reduced and the laptop cooled relatively quickly once I stopped the stress test. 

Bottom line, the entire package screams quality, efficiency, and a build that doesn't back down to your toughest multi-tasking needs. This laptop gives me the confidence to run a 3d print render while working on an excel workbook and chatting up the Copilot+ AI tool and not think twice about crashing any of the applications.

reviews.title: Fantastic upgrade from my 2022 Zenbook
reviews.content:
I have been so pleasantly surprised by the ASUS Zenbook A16 16" 3K OLED Touch Screen Laptop with Snapdragon X2 Elite Extreme (2026), 48GB RAM, 512GB SSD, Copilot+ PC, in Zabriskie Beige.

Having previously reviewed and used the flip-screen version of this laptop, this feels like a very welcome upgrade and update. The flip-screen model was an awesome concept, but ultimately, I wasn't convinced there was much longevity in that particular design. It was innovative and fun to use, but there were some trade-offs. I have much higher hopes for this new model.

Gone is the metallic construction and dual-use screen. While those were neat concepts, they also made the previous laptop surprisingly heavy. This new A16 is a completely different experience at just 2.65 pounds. That is incredibly light for a 16-inch laptop, and you really notice it the moment you pick it up.

You can't help but think ASUS is competing with Apple a little bit with this new form factor. And honestly, I'm completely on board with that. The material has a soft, almost velvety feel to it while still feeling solid and hardened enough to give you confidence that this isn't some fragile ultralight machine. The Zabriskie Beige color also gives it a premium look without being overly flashy.

The keyboard is terrific, and the trackpad is equally good for general browsing and everyday use. Everything feels well thought out, and there isn't much here that feels like a compromise simply because ASUS wanted to make the laptop thinner and lighter.

Then there is the battery life, which has honestly been one of the biggest surprises for me. I've only charged this laptop once since receiving it, and I'm still sitting at over half a charge after more than a week of casual use. That's with regular use during the day and routinely powering it down overnight. For something this thin and light, that's pretty impressive.

Gaming has also been a pleasant surprise. Let me be clear: this is not a dedicated gaming laptop, and I wouldn't recommend buying it if gaming is your primary reason for purchasing a computer. However, the Snapdragon X2 Elite Extreme and integrated Adreno graphics are considerably more capable than I expected. For casual gaming, it does a very respectable job, and the 120Hz 3K OLED display makes games look absolutely fantastic.

There is one important caveat with gaming, though. This is a Windows-on-ARM machine, so game compatibility isn't quite as straightforward as it is on a traditional Intel or AMD Windows laptop. Some games run surprisingly well, while others may have issues because they aren't optimized for ARM or rely on anti-cheat software that doesn't play nicely with the platform. For me, that's not a deal breaker. I'm not looking at this as a gaming rig. The fact that it can handle some gaming reasonably well is simply a really nice bonus.

Overall, I'm genuinely impressed with what ASUS has done here. The previous flip-screen model had a great concept, but this feels like a much more mature and practical direction. It's lighter, beautifully built, has an incredible OLED display, a great keyboard and trackpad, excellent battery life, and more performance than you might expect from something this thin and light.

I'm still putting it through its paces, so I'll be interested to see how it holds up over the long term. But after more than a week with it, my first impressions are extremely positive.

ASUS may have a real winner here. This feels less like a laptop trying to impress you with a gimmick and more like a laptop that simply gets the important things right. And honestly, that's a refreshing change.

reviews.title: Outstanding value and quality
reviews.content:
I waited a bit to write the review to see how it would perform over time. I've had it for about 6 months now and it's been fantastic - no issues whatsoever. It's being used with a MacBook Pro for a home office and normal office tasks - not media work.

The VESA mount works well, no installation issues. I am not using the provided stand so cannot speak to that. But mounts are not a big investment and improve the ergonomics of any monitor.

Screen quality is great, especially if you work with a lot of white background documents. White is uniform across screen, no moire patterns, no dim areas, no white hue transitions etc. Looks beautiful. I purchased a more expensive LG monitor which had noticeable patterns and I ended up returning that one and picked up this one. Saved money and got a better product. I was on the fence about returning that one because I thought maybe all screens have minor issues - nope, this one looks crystal clear.

The built in speakers are a nice addition. I sometimes listen to Pandora or NPR or podcasts in the background and they are perfectly nice - pls don't expect Bose performance form a monitor speaker.

Can't speak to the negative experiences of the other buyers here but I have not had any of the issues mentioned. I have no negatives to mention. I actually like everything about this monitor.

q_a.question: Are there an geographic restrictions to where this Windows 11 LIcense can be activated and used. I'm interested in buy this laptop as a gift for someone who resides in another country?
q_a.answer: The Windows license built into a computer travels with it and is valid anywhere in the world. It is permanently injected into the motherboard's physical hardware chips by the factory, it is not region-locked, and Microsoft will automatically activate it over the internet whether you boot it up in Europe, Asia, Africa, or the Americas. If purchased in another country, however, you may not be able to change the language if you travel outside that country without an additional cost. Also, if you are concerned about MS365 (formerly Office), that IS Region-Locked. it will often fail to activate if your Microsoft Account's location or IP address points to a different continent. Finally, while Lenovo includes an International Warranty Service (IWS) on many machines, it has severe limitations: Lenovo will only repair your laptop in another country if that exact model variant is also officially sold and supported by Lenovo in that destination country, and because your IdeaPad is a US-market consumer model, a Lenovo repair facility in another country may refuse to service it simply because they do not stock the US-spec replacement motherboards or keyboards.

reviews.title: Great Laptop with minor caveats
reviews.content:
With the current electronic market I do feel like it's very hard to find a perfect laptop under $2k but this is a very good option. I use this for personal web browsing and art with light gaming.

Let me start with the cons of this laptop. The main issues I have with the laptop are due to the configurations available at Bestbuy. 
1. There is no option for 1tb of storage for this model. 512gb is simply not enough storage for most people long term. Add on the fact that Lenovo + the Windows AI crap has a bunch of nonsense apps loaded on by default and after the initial system updates, you start off with about 80gb of your storage used up as soon as you boot it up. There is not an additional slot on the mobo to upgrade this btw you will have to get an external drive down the line.
2. There is no option for the 120hz model(for some reason, this option is just not available in the US??) I feel like in 2026 a 60hz screen on a system over $1k is a bit ridiculous. Odds are your phone has 120hz (my ipad from 2020 even has 120hz screen). Considering the amount of power in the CPU it also feels like a waste. Another issue is during the day the screen simply does not get bright enough. The screen is also super glossy so the glare you get is insane if you use it in a bright environment. 
3. The pen is not included and also not sold at bestbuy. I can understand for most people this is a non issue but I feel like by not even having the option I am missing out on an entire feature of the laptop. (I ended up getting one separately and it’s good for light art and notetaking [not practical for notetaking because of the laptop size] but while the pen is great there’s some weird windows software issues that pop up and cause lagging issues)
This is a nitpick but the charging cord is a bit short for me personally and unfortunately the cord is embedded into the block so if I wanted a longer cord I would have to get a 65watt block and cord. Also coming from a gaming laptop to me the laptop is light but to others it might be heavy.

Onto the Pros, this laptop is FAST, with 24GB of RAM and the intel i7 chip you can multitask and do work without being slowed down by your system. If you’re like me and tend to have a lot of things open at once this is fantastic. The laptop can also handle some light gaming, I played some Fields of Mistria, Stardew, and Spirit City and they all ran fine after adjusting some settings. I will say the 60hz screen definitely was noticeable to me while gaming(it makes things feel like there’s motion blur on). If you’re prone to motion sickness I’d be aware of that; you can change some settings to help but at the end of the day it will still be a 60hz screen. The color accuracy on this laptop is great, a bit oversaturated but good enough for me to continue doing my art. The keyboard is the best I’ve ever used on a laptop; I really like it(but it is a bit of a fingerprint magnet with hand oils). The fans are very quiet and the laptop barely even gets warm for me even when I gamed. The battery life for me has been great and lasts me all day but I don’t travel as much as others so I haven’t used it on battery alone for anything outside of web browsing.

Looks amazing and premium. The OLED screen is beautiful, wonderful colors, true blacks and glossy. It is also very lightweight and easy to carry around. reviews.title: Great specs for the price, but ultimately returned
reviews.content:
Bought this for the great specs at a great price point, but ultimately the cons outweighed that pro and I had to return this.

I primarily use a gaming laptop to hook up to various TVs around my house or on trips for mobile gaming. The cooling fans are so loud that I can barely hear the game above them, and had to raise the volume of my TV substantially. You are able to set the max fan speeds to a lower level, but when I did this, nothing seemed to happen. They were just loud, no matter what setting I tried.

I downloaded and played Red Dead Redemption 2, and it was unplayable because it would freeze-lag for 1-2 seconds at a time randomly, and when I got into a more intense gunfight, the game crashed completely to desktop. I lowered the graphics settings to almost the minimum and it still lagged. I spent hours trying to troubleshoot why this this laptop that was great on paper would struggle with a 2018 game. I couldn't fathom why there wasn't a silly, software or driver-based reason and solution for this. But nothing I tried worked.

I ultimately decided that, whether these problems were fixable or not, it wasn't acceptable to need to spend hours scouring forums trying solutions to fix serious performance issues to even make the laptop usable. I ultimately returned this to Best Buy after a few days.

I'm still giving 3 stars mainly because I suspect that I got a lemon. My time on help forums showed me that most people were able to fix their issues or had no issues at all out of the box. I unfortunately was not one of those people.

reviews.title: An Open Box Winner
reviews.content:
I picked this up open box at my local store.  The condition was "Open Box Good".  The laptop was in excellent condition.  It was marked "Good" and not excellent because there was no documentation.  Missing documentation didn't bother me at all, as this machine still had the original box and the charger.
I added a second NVME SSD, upgraded the RAM to 32 GB and upgraded to Windows 11 Pro.  At retail price, I would not recommend, because even though it's still lower in cost than comparable laptops, it's still expensive.  However, if available as "Open Box" at a local store and you're able to go and see the machine, boot it and make sure it works as intended, it is an absolute value in an open box state.  The reason for this is there are variants of this machine with similar specs that are equipped with a 240 Hz OLED display.
I use this laptop for web browsing, online training courses and light gaming.
Recommendation: if possible, elevate the rear of the laptop, so the fans can get the proper amount of air.  Otherwise, the fans will make a strange humming noise.  It annoyed me at first, but once I elevated the rear of the machine, the humming of the fans when gaming stopped.

reviews.title: Great hardware and value, messy Lenovo software
reviews.content:
I bought the 11-inch Lenovo Idea Tab with 8GB RAM, 128GB storage, Tab Pen and folio case as a birthday gift for a five-year-old who had already outgrown the idea of a basic “kids tablet.” For the price, the hardware package is excellent.

The 2.5K display is sharp and looks very good, performance has been smooth, and 8GB of RAM with 128GB of storage gives it plenty of room to grow. The included pen and folio case add real value instead of feeling like throwaway accessories. It also runs the full Google Play Store and works well with Google Family Link, which was important because I wanted a normal Android tablet that could still be properly supervised.

The biggest negative is Lenovo’s software setup. It came with quite a few unnecessary apps and games installed, and there are a lot of Lenovo-specific menus, gestures, multitasking features and settings that took time to sort through and disable or configure. Some of those features are useful for an experienced user, but they make the initial setup more complicated than it needs to be, especially when configuring the tablet for a child.

Once everything was updated and configured, though, it became a very capable tablet. I would much rather have this than a heavily restricted kids tablet that would be outgrown quickly.

Pros: sharp display, 8GB RAM, 128GB storage, expandable storage, full Android/Google Play support, pen and folio included, good parental-control support.

Cons: too much preinstalled software, unnecessarily complicated Lenovo settings, requires some cleanup during initial setup.

For the price paid, I’m very satisfied with it and think it offers a lot more long-term usefulness than most tablets marketed specifically toward children.

q_a.question: Is the laptop compatible with all HP docking stations?
q_a.answer: Since both types are made by HP, OF COURSE they will be compatible with each other. However, a docking station will not magically give the computer an ability it would not have otherwise. For example, the USB-C ports on the laptop have 10Gbps signalling rate; if the docking station supports 20Gbps (or greater) connectivity, you will not suddenly have 20Gbps available to you.

reviews.title: A Laptop That Exceeded My Expectations!
reviews.content:
I absolutely love my HP OmniBook X Flip! I had been looking for a laptop that could handle school, work, multitasking, and everyday use while still feeling premium and enjoyable to use, and this laptop has exceeded my expectations.

The 16" 2K OLED touchscreen is easily one of my favorite features. The display is absolutely beautiful, with vibrant colors, excellent contrast, and plenty of screen space for having multiple windows open. Everything from working on documents and spreadsheets to watching movies looks fantastic. The touchscreen and 2-in-1 design are also incredibly convenient and make the laptop much more versatile.

Performance has been excellent so far. The Intel Core Ultra 5, 16GB of memory, and 512GB SSD make everyday tasks feel fast and responsive, even when I have multiple applications and browser tabs open at the same time. I also really appreciate having Copilot+ features built in.

The Eclipse Gray finish gives it a sleek, professional look, and the overall build quality makes it feel like a much more expensive laptop. I especially appreciate that it manages to combine a large, gorgeous display with the flexibility of a 2-in-1.

As a college student, this has been an especially great fit for me. It gives me the screen real estate I want for school and work without sacrificing the features and flexibility that make it enjoyable to use every day.

Overall, I am extremely happy with this purchase. The combination of the OLED display, performance, touchscreen, 2-in-1 design, and premium feel makes this one of the best laptops I've owned. I would absolutely recommend the HP OmniBook X Flip to anyone looking for a powerful, versatile, and genuinely enjoyable laptop!

reviews.title: Excellent Battery Life and Screen... but 60hz
reviews.content:
Real world battery life is fantastic. Without making any effort to conserve battery, I was getting roughly 2 hours for every 10% drop in battery life during light use (web browsing with Chrome, watching videos) with balanced power settings in Windows. Really liked the small, lightweight power brick that can still add a decent amount of charge in a short time. The keyboard is very good, in my opinion, and much improved over the totally flat version in the previous generation. Touchscreen works well, and it's pretty fun to use as a comically large tablet when kicking back on the couch. Speakers are good enough to get the job done, but my expectations for laptop speakers are pretty low though so take that for what you will. 

16 gigs of memory and a 512GB SSD feel inadequate for the price, but given how expensive memory and storage have become I suppose those amounts are actually reasonable. Regardless, both are enough for the sort of lightweight tasks the rest of the hardware is suited to anyway. The OLED display really wows with its contrast especially, but a 60hz refresh rate feels inadequate in 2026. I haven't purchased a display with less than 120hz in 10+ years at this point, so the lack of smoothness feels very noticeable to me even just scrolling websites etc.

I ended up returning this one, in spite of the fact that I really liked it overall. Why? Well, it went on sale for over $200 less than I paid for it, and Best Buy could not (would not?) price match the difference because I traded in my old laptop at the same time... but I could still return it. Was planning to just buy the same one again for $200 less, but then found the substantially upgraded model with double the ram, storage, and a 3k 120hz OLED on sale for a couple hundred more than I paid originally. So I went with that one instead.

Compared to other laptops with these kinds of specs, it’s light and portable, and the fan is relatively quiet. The keyboard is excellent - satisfyingly clicky without that gummy feeling you get from a lot of gaming laptops. The undercarriage gets a little toasty while running GPU intensive games, so don’t plan on using it directly on your lap. It’s expensive, yes, but not compared to similar models from other makers. 

All in all, this laptop is one of the best I’ve ever owned
