I wanted something sleek, portable, and highly capable of handling both gaming and content creation. I can confidently say the Stealth 16 AI+ checks every single box.

If you’re currently cross-shopping other laptops like the G16, I highly recommend giving this one a shot. For starters, it’s about $400 cheaper while offering double the storage and upgradeable RAM. Sure, the GPU power (TGP) is a bit lower than the G16, but you really have to ask yourself if a slight performance bump is worth an extra $400. For me, gaming performance has been fantastic, it handles everything from Lego Batman to Forza Horizon 6 like a champ. The build quality is solid, it looks incredibly clean, and it's exactly what I was looking for.

The only catch: My first unit arrived with a rattling trackpad and a creaky hinge. I exchanged it, and the replacement unit is absolutely rock solid.

If you’re looking for a powerful, “stealthy” laptop for gaming, content creation, and daily work, you should definitely take a look at this one.

q_a.question: does it come with the pen? if not what is a compatible one?
q_a.answer: No, this laptop doesn't come with a Stylus pen. It is compatible with MPP 2.0 or 2.6, like the ASUS Pen 2.0 (SA203H) and ASUS Pen (SA205H), or third-party MPP 2.0 or MPP 2.0 Stylus pen.

q_a.question: I saw the storage was upgradable. What size M.2 is it? And does it fit dual sided or single sided only NVMEs?
q_a.answer: This ProArt PX13 (HN7306EA) laptop uses a compact M.2 2230 (22mm x 30mm) form factor for its NVMe PCIe 4.0 x4 SSD slot. It fits single-sided NVMe SSDs only due to surface-mounted components positioned close to the motherboard's M.2 slot, dual-sided SSDs will not have enough physical clearance and will not fit safely.

q_a.question: Can you add storage to this later on?
q_a.answer: Yes, you can upgrade the internal storage on this ProArt PX13 (HN7306EA) laptop by replacing the existing drive, but you cannot add a second drive because there is only one M.2 slot.

q_a.question: Is there a screen protector that doesn’t affect the touchscreen sensitivity
q_a.answer: Yes, there are ultra-thin plastic film screen protectors designed specifically for the ProArt PX13 laptop from third-party seller that maintain touchscreen sensitivity without hindering touch or stylus response.

q_a.question: Can It able to work with Linux distros like Fedora KDE, Kali Linux for network and cybersecurity?
q_a.answer: Yes, the ASUS ProArt PX13 (model HN7306EA) can work with Linux distributions like Fedora KDE and Kali Linux, but you will need a very new Linux kernel (v6.12 or newer) for proper hardware support.

q_a.question: How many external monitors can this laptop support?
q_a.answer: The ASUS ProArt PX13 (model HN7306EA) laptop can support up to three external monitors simultaneously, in addition to its built-in display. The laptop has two USB 4.0 Gen 3 Type-C ports that support display output and one HDMI 2.1 port for native monitor connections.

q_a.question: What is the Wattage (100% GPU/CPU) used total? Can it be charged using USB C?
q_a.answer: This specific laptop model has a combined CPU and GPU maximum thermal design power (TDP) of roughly 115 W to 120 W. Yes, the laptop can be charged using a USB-C charger. However, there are limitations, the USB-C port supports up to 100 W of Power Delivery (PD). If you are gaming or rendering videos at 100% capacity, a 100 W USB-C charger will not be able to fully run the laptop on maximum settings. During these heavy tasks, the system may occasionally dip into the battery for extra power. USB-C charger is perfect for charging while the laptop is in sleep mode.

q_a.question: Does this come with a pen? If not, what pens are compatible and where are they in stock at Best Buy stores?
q_a.answer: It works with my Microsoft Surface pen (but did not work with the Lenovo).

description: BUILT FOR COLLEGE. AND BEYOND — MacBook Air with the M5 chip packs blazing speed and powerful AI capabilities into an incredibly portable design. And with up to 18 hours of battery life,¹ this thin and light powerhouse is ready to take on almost any major, just about anywhere.

TEAR THROUGH TOUGH ASSIGNMENTS — With its faster CPU and unified memory, the M5 chip delivers even more performance and fluidity across apps, making multitasking and creative workflows smooth and responsive. A powerful Neural Engine and next-generation GPU with Neural Accelerators give you a powerful platform for AI.

MAKE QUICK WORK OF YOUR TO-DO LIST — Apple Intelligence helps you write, express yourself, and get things done effortlessly — whether it’s for school or everyday life. With groundbreaking privacy protections, it gives you peace of mind that no one else can access your data — not even Apple. ²
UP TO 18 HOURS OF BATTERY LIFE¹ — MacBook Air delivers incredible battery life with amazing performance, so you can power through a full day of classes without worrying about plugging in.

A BRILLIANT 15.3-INCH DISPLAY³ — The gorgeous Liquid Retina display on MacBook Air supports 1 billion colors, making photos and videos pop with rich contrast and sharp detail, and text appears supercrisp. So everything — from class presentations to movies to games — looks truly stunning.

LOOK AND SOUND YOUR BEST — Automatically stay in frame during online classes and video calls with the 12MP Center Stage camera, or use Desk View to share a top-down view of your workspace with classmates. And the three-mic array and six-speaker sound system with Spatial Audio and support for Dolby Atmos make everything sound great.

MAKE POWERFUL CONNECTIONS — MacBook Air features two Thunderbolt 4 ports, a MagSafe charging port, a headphone jack, and the Apple N1 wireless chip for Wi-Fi 7⁯ and Bluetooth 6. Plus, it supports up to two external displays. So you can set up your workstation just how you like it.

MACOS RUNS APPS FAST — All your go-to apps run lightning fast in macOS, including built-in apps like FaceTime⁵ and Messages. Plus, built-in virus protection and free software updates help keep your Mac running smoothly and securely.⁶

MAC AND IPHONE. EVEN BETTER TOGETHER — Mac and iPhone are amazing on their own. And they’re even more amazing when used together. See and control what’s on your iPhone right from your Mac.⁶ Start an email on one device and finish it on the other. Snap a photo on your iPhone and see it appear on your Mac. Or make a call without ever reaching for your iPhone.⁷

reviews.title: Mac Book Air Fan!!!
reviews.content:
My last laptop was an LG Gram, I loved that computer but was damaged due to water spilled on it.  While looking for a new lap top, I started researching the top ones to get, Apple Macbook Air came on top on every list. I dove into the research further, and one concern I had was making the jump from windows to the apple environment.  I already own and use apple phones and ipads, so maybe it will be all ok, and it was.    On a side note, I have had an 2018 Ipad pro, and although its getting a little slow, it still works great.  Also, I have several old laptops around the house, all that seems to slow down after 18 mos to 3 yrs.    

I bought the 24 gb version, 1 tb HD, and used it for 2 weeks, and was immedicably impressed.   
no bloatware
no ads asking me to renew the virus checker
No fan noise
MS office installs seamlessly 
I have all my  favorites in one place
I love the fingerprint reader
battery last a really long time
i love the 15" screen, and do not miss the 17" touch screen i had before

If you are on the fence, and want a lap top that will last a really long time the differences between windows and apple are very few, and well worth the time to learn it.

reviews.title: Perfect Laptop for a College Student!
reviews.content:
I purchased the Apple MacBook Air 15-inch for my daughter as she started her first year of college as a freshman, and she absolutely loves it! From the moment she started using it, she was impressed with how lightweight and easy it is to carry around, especially for a college student who is constantly moving between classes.

The MacBook Air has so many features and capabilities that she didn’t even realize she would need or appreciate. It’s fast, reliable, easy to use, and feels very durable. Most importantly, it has everything she needs for schoolwork, studying, projects, and everyday use.

As a parent, I wanted to make sure I purchased something that would last—not something she would outgrow after a year or two. After seeing how much she enjoys using it and how well it performs, I feel this was a great investment that should serve her throughout her college years and beyond.

I highly recommend the 15-inch MacBook Air to any college student or parent looking for a reliable, lightweight, and long-lasting laptop. **Definitely a purchase we’re very happy with!**

I recently purchased this computer, and so far, my overall experience with it has been pretty good. The computer does exactly what I expected it to do, and I haven’t really had any major problems with it. Setting everything up was simple and didn’t take very long. Once it was ready, the computer started up quickly and everything seemed to work normally.

The performance is good for everyday use. I’ve used it for browsing the internet, watching videos, doing schoolwork, opening different programs, and just doing regular computer stuff. Everything runs smoothly, and I haven’t noticed any serious lag or slowdown. The screen looks nice and clear, and the keyboard feels comfortable enough to type on for longer periods of time.

The design is also pretty nice. It looks modern without being too complicated or flashy. The computer feels well made and doesn’t feel cheap. Battery life seems decent, although it obviously depends on what you’re doing.

Overall, it’s a computer that computers very well. It turns on, runs programs, connects to the internet, and successfully performs computer-related activities. If you need a computer to do computer things, this is definitely one of the computers available.

After just a few years, I was one of many users that reported issues with hinges breaking, making the laptops difficult or impossible to use. So I suddenly needed a new laptop, but I wanted one that was comparable to what I had.
My new Acer laptop is a noticeable improvement over my old HP Envy 2-in-1, it offers faster performance, quicker startup and application loading, smoother multitasking and a more responsive overall experience. It also provides a newer, more efficient design with improved battery life, better connectivity and a more comfortable setup for my everyday tasks such as browsing, streaming, writing and video calls. While the HP Envy’s convertible touchscreen design was convenient, my new Acer outperforms it in speed, responsiveness and day-to-day efficiency. I will never buy an HP again.

reviews.title: Lenovo hit the idea with this laptop
reviews.content:
I bought two of these and they’ve been solid daily drivers. This configuration stands out in the affordable 15-inch range thanks to the 120Hz touchscreen and 16GB of RAM, two features that make a real difference in everyday use.

What’s good

The 15.3-inch 1920×1200 IPS touchscreen (16:10) with 120Hz refresh is the highlight. Scrolling, window dragging, and general navigation feel noticeably smoother than typical 60Hz budget panels. Once you switch it to 120Hz in display settings (it may ship set to 60Hz), everything feels more responsive. Brightness is good for indoor and shaded outdoor use, and colors look properly saturated for casual work and media.
The Intel Core 7 350 paired with 16GB DDR5 handles heavy multitasking without drama, dozens of browser tabs, documents, streaming, messaging, and video calls all at once stayed smooth. The 512GB PCIe 4.0 SSD is quick for everyday file work. Memory is upgradeable (one SODIMM slot, up to 32GB), which is a nice future proofing touch.

Battery life is practical. In mixed real-world use I saw roughly 9.5–11+ hours depending on whether I left it at 120Hz or dropped to 60Hz. Rapid Charge Boost is useful—about 15 minutes on the included 65W charger restores a couple hours of light use. USB-C Power Delivery also works with compatible chargers.

Ports are better than most thin laptops at this price: two USB A, one USB C (with PD and DisplayPort), HDMI, full size SD card reader, and audio jack. No constant dongle hunting. The keyboard is quiet and comfortable for long typing sessions, and the touchpad is reliable. Build is solid plastic (Cosmic Blue on mine), around 3.5 lbs, and it slides into my laptop bag without issue. Hinge is steady and the finish has held up fine with daily carry.

What’s not perfect

No keyboard backlight is the biggest miss for evening use. The 720p webcam is adequate for calls but nothing special (it does have a physical privacy shutter, which is good). Fan noise stays reasonable under load, and the underside can get warm during heavy sessions, so desk use is more comfortable than lap use for longer periods.

Bottom line

At the price I paid, this exact trim (Core 7 350 + 16GB + 120Hz touchscreen) delivers strong everyday performance, a smooth display, solid battery, and practical connectivity without feeling compromised. It’s not a flashy premium machine, but it’s reliable, capable, and easy to live with day after day. I’m happy with both units and would buy them again for general productivity, browsing, media, and multitasking.

reviews.title: Missing correct power supply
reviews.content:
The laptop seemed fine, the issue was the incorrect power supply was in the packaging.  This was a Open Box/Excellent deal.  I went to my local Best Buy to replace the PS and was told I needed to take the Insignia brand as a replacement.  Due to the cost of the laptop even with the discount, I wanted the specific PS that came with it.  The Manager told me I could buy the Extended Warranty for over $200 and get a new one that way.  He also suggested I could drive another 30 miles to the next store and see if they would swap out the PS on the open box they had in stock (He currently didn't have one).  However due to Best Buys new policies, you can't contact individual stores to find out if they would agree to that.

I got the impression while talking with the Manager that Best Buy is a bunch of fragmented individual stores that only help you if you purchased directly through that particular location.  So my only options being take an off brand PS, drive another 30 miles to next store, or return the item, I elected to return it.  Not the best outcome for my daughter who needs a higher end laptop for her engineering classes.  I also asked about trading it for a Brand New one and was immediately shut down, without even discussing paying up for it.  FYI the location I went to was Alamo Ranch.

reviews.content:
I don't travel, so the laptop stays plugged in all the time, so can't speak to battery life or portability.  However, the laptop is somewhat heavy, just a note there.

I started a clean slate with this laptop (and upgraded to Pro).  However, there seems to be some oddity with the mouse and typing being a bit stuttering.  Other things, too.

I got this because I'm a power user and like to have different programs open at the same time, but currently?  It's not smoooooth sailing.  Might be because the laptop and I are just getting used to each other?  Might be due to me using an usb port hub that doesn't have 2.0 usb ports for my mouse and keyboard? I've ordered a new usb port hub that does have 2 2.0 usb ports, arrives soon.  I'll find out if that's the issue or not.

But as to the laptop being SLOW to open programs - not so sure about that right now - I'm working to figure that out because I know AMD Radeon graphics are excellent and so is AMD Ryzer AI 9.  Plus 32 GB RAM.  Nothing should be slow at all.  But clearly something is happening.  Maybe defective components?  Don't know - will be testing things to figure that out.

Overall, if I ignore the slow response of opening programs - I'd say this is a good laptop to get.  I can't say it's a great laptop at this point.  If I can return to provide an update, I will do that.

reviews.title: Excellent laptop
reviews.content:
I really liked this laptop despite the fact that I returned it. I will explain the pros and the ultimate reason why I returned it. I am a niche user, the user this is intended for would LOVE it. 

Pro: 
+ 32GB RAM, it is too easy to run up against 16GB RAM limits that I dont consider anything without 32GB. My desktops have 64GB but I admit they never go past 24GB of use for what I do. 
+ Great build quality, you can lift from a corner and don't feel it flex
+ Great screen and accurate touchscreen
+ Sound/speakers are better than 98% of laptops out there
+ Great performance for this class of CPU
++ Single core performance is great, snappy system
++ Multicore performance is above average for this class of CPU
+ iGPU/graphics being the 880M from AMD is solid, not great for gaming but you can even get Fortnite going at a decent experience for a non-gaming laptop
+ USB-C charging, basically a must for me now 
+ Keyboard key travel is short in a good way. Seems a little shorter travel than the Zephyrus series but more than my Samsung Book5 pro. I prefer the shorter Samsung but this was good for I think more users. 

Cons-
- While I listed the iGPU in the Pro, it was a downgrade from my Samsung Book5 Pro 14" with the intel ARC 140V iGPU in the Intel Ultra 7 258V CPU (series 2)
- This is not used for gaming often but when I go out of town, I do use it to play Fortnite with two sons, the 880M was noticeably behind the Intel 140V. I still got the game to play well enough, highs over 100fps but every now n then there would be a stutter. 
- Fans are not loud but could be a bit better, if I chose to keep it I planned to change the thermal paste to Thermal Grizzly TG PhaseSheet PTM which did wonders on my Samsung laptop.
- Keyboard keycaps can be a little slippery. I like when keycaps have a little grip to them. Personal preference thing. 

Overall, this is an excellent chassis and a complete package for most people shopping this type of laptop. I wish Asus made it with the Intel Ultra x7 or x9 CPU series 3 CPU with Intel ARC B390, I would purchase again if they did so.

reviews.title: Best Laptop I've Ever Owned
reviews.content:
Huge upgrade from my previous gaming laptop. The battery is awesome, it comfortably lasts a full 8-hour workday of mixed activities like office work and streaming. The OLED display is amazing and can get really bright. The speakers are surprisingly good. The build quality is solid, durable, and it's super light, thin, and very portable. The performance is great for most tasks as well. And the charging brick isn't an actual BRICK for a change! It's like a phone charger and it's so convenient to carry around. Well worth the price! 

Some nitpicks:
 - Wish the screen was matte instead of glossy, the reflections can be a little annoying for apps in dark mode
 - Although the touchpad is great and high quality, the huge size causes you to accidentally click on the wrong thing often when you're in the middle of typing. It definitely takes some time to adjust

A great choice overall and I would recommend this to my friends and family in a heartbeat!

reviews.title: Great laptop, bad Best Buy delivery
reviews.content: Great computer, no complaints with the computer but Best Buy service and delivery process is not the best. I purchased this laptop on a weekend. Notifications said the delivery was the following Wednesay via UPS Roadie courier. I skipped some appointments and came home early. The Roadie notifications showed the laptop was delivered just before I got home. In my driveway was a Best Buy sealed box that should have contained the laptop and a keyboard. When I opened the box, no computer, just the keyboard. When you try to contact Best Buy customer service, the store can't help and the online resource dosent tell you what to do about a missing item. They only provide options for support of the product once you have it. I spent hours asking the Best Buy chat for support but got nowhere. Luckily my wife works as customer support for another company and started asking for a manager. After that, we got in touch with a real person (still not a manager) via the chat tool who was understanding. I was ready to file a police report as the computer is more than $500 and the box was sealed when I got it but the agent insistend a report was unnessary and a replacement laptop would be sent. The next day, Thursday I received a notification about the replacmement delivering to me the next Sunday. I waited patiently until Sunday. Sunday morning I received a notification that the delivery was delayed. LSince I was not far from the store in Cumming Ga where the laptop was coming from I thought I would make things easier and pick it up myself. I got to the store and the people there could not help me. I was there for about 40 - 60 minutes. I was told there was a system error showing on the store end and there was nothing that could be done for me. I went back home l, went online, started the Best Buy chat tool and asked for another manager. The agent ( not a manager), said they thought there was an inventory or process error and reset the order for store pickup. About midday the following Monday the laptop was confirmed ready. I finally picked it up later that Monday. When I decided to buy from Best Buy, I did so because I didnt trust Amazon's delivery process. Best Buy let me down. I am happy things worked out in the end but this purchase took way more of my time than it should have. I will be very hesitant to purchase from Best Buy again.
